title: Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's

title: Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS)
description: The Ontario Graduate Scholarship (OGS) is a merit-based scholarship program jointly funded by the Province of Ontario (two-thirds) and participating Ontario universities (one-third). It encourages excellence in graduate studies at the master's and doctoral levels across all academic disciplines.
deadline_display: Varies by host university (typically November 2026 – March 2027 for the 2027-2028 academic year)
verification_notes: Enriched with official Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities guidelines, U of T SGS regulations, and provincial allocation rules.
duration: 1 year (2 or 3 consecutive terms; renewable up to a maximum lifetime duration)
application_period: Annual competition cycle; internal deadlines set individually by each participating Ontario university
official_source: School of Graduate Studies, University of Toronto / Ontario Ministry of Colleges and Universities
eligibility: Canadian citizens, Permanent Residents, or Protected Persons under subsection 95(2) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (Canada)
International students holding a valid Canadian Study Permit by the institutional application deadline
Enrolled or planning to enroll full-time in an eligible Master's or Doctoral graduate program at a participating Ontario university
Achieved a minimum average of A- (80% / 3.7+ GPA out of 4.0) in EACH of the last two completed years of full-time academic study
Must not have exceeded the lifetime maximum of 6 years of government-funded graduate award support (including OGS, QEII-GSST, SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR)
eligibility_summary: Open to high-achieving domestic and international graduate students enrolled full-time in Master's or PhD programs at participating Ontario universities, maintaining an A- average in their last two years of study.
benefits: $15,000 maximum per academic year ($5,000 per consecutive term for up to 3 terms)
$10,000 for 2 consecutive terms
Joint funding structure: $10,000 provided by the Province of Ontario and $5,000 matched by the host university
coverage: Direct cash award / stipend credited toward university tuition account or disbursed as living allowance
Does not include separate health insurance, airfare, or research travel grants
requirements: Direct submission of OGS application to the specific department/graduate unit at the participating Ontario university
Demonstrated academic excellence (transcripts showing A- minimum in the last 2 study years)
Strong research ability and potential as demonstrated through proposal and publications
Two confidential academic reference reports using official OGS referee forms
documents: Official OGS Application Form (completed via the host university portal)
Official Academic Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended
Two Academic Reference Letters / OGS Confidential Assessment Reports
Statement of Intent / Research Proposal (1-2 pages)
List of Academic Honors, Scholarships, Awards, and Peer-Reviewed Publications (CV/Resume)
Proof of Canadian Citizenship, PR status, or valid Study Permit (for international applicants)
english_requirement: Applicants must meet the official English language proficiency requirements of the host Ontario university and department where the award is held (e.g., IELTS Academic overall 7.0+ or TOEFL iBT 93–100+ depending on institution).
application_method: Identify the participating Ontario university (e.g., U of T, Waterloo, McMaster, Western, York, Ottawa) where you intend to hold the scholarship
Access the host university's graduate awards portal and select the OGS application option
Upload transcripts, research statement, and nominate two academic referees
Submit before the host university's internal department deadline
selection_notes: Adjudicated locally by faculty review committees at each university based on: Academic Excellence (40%), Research Ability and Potential (30%), and Communication/Leadership Skills (30%). Each university has a fixed allocation quota for domestic and international students.
best_fit: Outstanding Master's and PhD students with strong academic records (A- average) pursuing full-time research or professional graduate degrees in Ontario.
notes: OGS awards are non-transferable between universities; an OGS awarded at University of Toronto cannot be transferred to University of Waterloo. International quotas are strictly limited (typically up to 5-10% of a university's total allocation).
_cycle: Annual provincial competition with university-specific internal deadlines

best_fit: High-achieving international research master's, doctoral students, and postdocs seeking fully funded research opportunities in Quebec, Canada.
notes: Recipients must reside physically in Quebec for the entire duration of the award. PBEEE cannot be held concurrently with Canadian federal scholarships (e.g., CGRS/Vanier) or other Quebec government awards, but can be combined with institutional top-ups or home country awards.
